name: Nonconformance through corrective and preventive action in regulated manufacturing
summary: When an inspector finds parts or devices that do not meet their specification, the plant must tag and segregate them, record what is wrong, check whether other stock is affected, and have a material review board decide whether to rework, scrap, use as is or return the material. The quality engineer then decides whether the problem needs a formal corrective and preventive action (CAPA), in which an engineer finds the root cause, changes the process and later checks over months that the problem has not come back. In a medical device plant every step is required by FDA's Quality System Regulation and ISO 13485, so each decision needs a named authority and a signed record. Much of the work is physical inspection, sorting, rework and shop-floor investigation, and most elapsed time is waiting for review boards, rework slots, suppliers, engineering changes and the effectiveness monitoring window.

baseline.org_archetype: A medical device manufacturer of about 600 people with one plant making machined, molded and assembled Class II devices, registered with FDA and certified to ISO 13485, using an ERP and either a basic eQMS or controlled paper forms for NCRs and CAPAs.
baseline.notes: One case is one nonconformance report. Most close after disposition with a recorded correction; about one in six becomes a formal CAPA.

unit_of_work: one nonconformance report and, where escalated, its CAPA
trigger: An inspector or operator finds product that does not conform to its specification during receiving, in-process or final inspection, or returned product is found nonconforming.
end_state: The material is dispositioned and the report closed with cause recorded; or, where a CAPA was opened, the actions are implemented, verified, shown to be effective and the CAPA is closed.

volume.seasonality: Rises after new product introductions, supplier changes and new hires; otherwise steady.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a 600-person device plant; no source opened gave nonconformance counts per plant.

triggered_by.from: In-process and final inspection in production
triggered_by.object: nonconforming work in progress or finished devices

triggered_by.from: Complaint handling and returned product evaluation

produces.object: released, reworked or scrapped material with ERP status
returned material and supplier corrective action request

produces.to: Complaint handling and field action process
produces.object: field risk assessment for shipped suspect lots
engineering change requests from corrective actions

systems.name: Quality management system records (eQMS or controlled paper NCR and CAPA forms)
ERP (inventory status, lots, scrap and return transactions)
NCR and CAPA logs and trend spreadsheets
Inspection gauges, CMM and test equipment

steps.name: Detect and tag nonconforming product
steps.description: During receiving, in-process or final inspection the quality inspector measures parts against the drawing or test limits, finds one or more out of tolerance or failing, stops the lot, attaches a red hold tag and notes what was found.

error.defect_description: Wrong characteristic or quantity noted, or a good part tagged because of a gauge error.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(a): identification, documentation, evaluation, segregation and disposition of nonconforming product (also ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.3)

evidence.note: Identification of nonconforming product is required by 820.90(a); severity grading from src8. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write nonconformance report
steps.description: The inspector opens a new nonconformance report in the quality system or on the paper form and records part number, lot, quantity, where found, the requirement, the measured value and photos, and links it to the traveler or device history record.

error.defect_description: Report missing the measured value, lot or quantity, so the engineer must go back to the floor.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(a): identification, documentation, evaluation, segregation and disposition of nonconforming product (also ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.3)

evidence.note: Documentation of the nonconformity is required by 820.90(a) and ISO 9001 8.7 (src2). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Move to quarantine and put on hold
steps.description: The inspector moves the tagged material to the locked MRB area and changes its status in the ERP to hold or nonconforming so it cannot be picked or shipped, recording the location on the report.

error.defect_description: ERP status not changed, so the material can still be allocated.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(a): identification, documentation, evaluation, segregation and disposition of nonconforming product (also ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.3)

evidence.note: Segregation is required by 820.90(a). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the nonconformance and set containment scope
steps.description: The quality engineer reads the report, looks at the parts in the MRB area, classifies severity, and decides whether other lots, work in progress or finished stock made the same way could be affected and need to be held and checked.

error.defect_description: Containment scope set too narrow, so suspect product stays in stock.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(a): identification, documentation, evaluation, segregation and disposition of nonconforming product (also ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.3)

next.condition: other lots or stock may be affected

evidence.note: Evaluation under 820.90(a); interim containment is D3 of 8D (src4) and a CAPA step in src5. The 25% sweep share and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Sort suspect stock and work in progress
steps.description: Inspectors pull every suspect lot from stock, work in progress and the finished goods area, inspect or test the affected characteristic, tag and quarantine the failures and record the counts on the report.

error.defect_description: Some suspect stock missed in a remote location.

evidence.note: Interim containment such as quarantining affected product (src4, src5). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check shipped product and field risk
steps.description: The quality engineer uses the device history records and ERP shipment history to see whether suspect lots have shipped, and if they have, records a risk assessment and refers the case to the complaint and field action process.

error.defect_description: Shipped lot missed because lot genealogy is incomplete.

evidence.note: Checking for escapes is a normal part of containment in device plants; times and frequency are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare MRB package
steps.description: The quality engineer gathers the measurements, drawing, the history of similar nonconformances from the log and, where useful, re-measures parts, then writes a proposed disposition for the material review board.

error.defect_description: History of repeat nonconformances not checked.

evidence.note: Review and disposition process set out under 820.90(b). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Material review board disposition
steps.description: At the twice-weekly material review board in the MRB area, the quality manager, quality engineer, manufacturing engineer and, when needed, design engineering and purchasing look at the parts and data and decide rework, scrap, use as is or return to supplier, signing the report. The time shown is total attendee time for this report.

error.defect_description: Rework chosen where it cannot restore conformity.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(b)(1): defined responsibility for review and authority for disposition, documented disposition (ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.7 and ISO 13485 clause 8.3)

next.condition: use as is, needs engineering justification

evidence.note: Disposition authority and records (820.90(b), ISO 9001 8.7). The disposition mix and meeting frequency are the author's estimate for a machined and assembled device plant.

steps.name: Write rework instruction
steps.description: The manufacturing engineer writes a rework instruction that says how the parts are to be reworked, what must be retested and how results are recorded, and gets it approved by quality.

error.defect_description: Instruction omits a retest of a characteristic affected by the rework.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(b)(2): rework procedures including retesting and reevaluation

evidence.note: Rework procedures are required by 820.90(b)(2). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Rework the parts
steps.description: A production operator takes the material from the MRB area, reworks each part on the line or a rework bench following the instruction, and logs quantities and time on the traveler.

error.defect_description: Parts reworked incorrectly or mixed with good parts.

evidence.note: Rework waits for a gap in the production schedule; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-inspect reworked parts
steps.description: The quality inspector re-measures or retests every reworked part against current specifications, records the results in the device history record and either releases them from hold in the ERP or sends failures back to the review board.

error.defect_description: Measurement error passes a bad part.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(b)(2): retest and reevaluate reworked product and document it in the device history record

next.condition: parts still nonconforming, back to MRB

evidence.note: Retesting and recording rework in the DHR is required by 820.90(b)(2). The 8% fail rate and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Justify use as is
steps.description: The sustaining design engineer analyses whether the deviation affects fit, function, safety or performance, using tolerance stack-ups, test data or risk files, and writes the technical justification that the regulation requires before nonconforming product can be used.

error.defect_description: Justification overlooks a use condition.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(b)(1): justification for use of nonconforming product and signature of the individuals authorising the use

evidence.note: Justification and signature for use of nonconforming product (820.90(b)(1)). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Scrap material and post the write-off
steps.description: The material handler takes the material to the scrap area, destroys or marks it so it cannot be reused, and posts the scrap transaction in the ERP against the report number so the cost is recorded.

error.defect_description: Scrap posted with wrong quantity or cost centre.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: inventory write-offs posted against an approved disposition

evidence.note: Scrap handling and ERP posting times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Return to supplier and request corrective action
steps.description: The buyer gets a return authorisation from the supplier, arranges shipment of the material back, issues a debit or replacement order, and sends the supplier a corrective action request with the report attached.

error.defect_description: Replacement order not placed, causing a shortage.

evidence.note: Waiting for the supplier's return authorisation and the buyer's effort are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether a CAPA is needed
steps.description: The quality engineer checks the nonconformance log for repeats of the same defect, weighs severity and risk, and decides whether the cause can be recorded with a simple correction or needs a formal corrective and preventive action.

error.defect_description: Repeat problem treated as a one-off, so it recurs.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(a): evaluation includes a determination of the need for an investigation; 820.100(a)(1) analysis of quality data to find recurring problems

next.condition: no CAPA needed: cause and correction recorded

evidence.note: Determination of the need for investigation (820.90(a)) and trend analysis of quality data (820.100(a)(1), src3). The 20% escalation rate is the author's estimate. FDA's Case for Quality review links better control of common manufacturing risks to fewer CAPAs and investigations (src6).

steps.name: Close the nonconformance report
steps.description: The quality engineer checks that the disposition is complete, ERP transactions are posted and records are attached, enters the cause code for trending and closes the report.

error.defect_description: Report closed with a disposition step not done.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.90(a): the evaluation and any investigation shall be documented (ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.7 records)

evidence.note: Documentation of evaluation and disposition (820.90, ISO 9001 8.7). The closure lag is the author's estimate.

steps.name: CAPA board accepts and assigns the CAPA
steps.description: The quality manager reviews the request at the weekly CAPA review board with engineering and operations leads, accepts or rejects it, assigns an owner and due dates and gives it a CAPA number. The time shown is total attendee time for this request.

error.defect_description: Owner assigned without time freed to do the work.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a): procedures for implementing corrective and preventive action (ISO 13485:2016 clauses 8.5.2 and 8.5.3)

next.condition: rejected as a CAPA; handled through the nonconformance report

evidence.note: Review board acceptance or rejection and tracking number (src5). Rejection share and board frequency are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Form team and define the problem
steps.description: The CAPA owner, usually the process engineer for the area, pulls together a small team, writes a measurable problem statement using what, where, when and how many, and lists the data needed.

error.defect_description: Problem statement restates a symptom, steering the investigation wrong.

evidence.note: Team and problem description (8D D1 and D2, src4); cross-functional team (src5). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate the root cause
steps.description: The CAPA owner observes the process on the shop floor, interviews operators, reviews travelers, maintenance and calibration records, measures samples and runs trials, then works through cause and effect diagrams and repeated why questions until a cause is supported by evidence.

error.defect_description: Cause named as operator error or a restated problem without evidence.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(2): investigate the cause of nonconformities

next.condition: supplier cause: supplier root cause needed

evidence.note: Cause investigation (820.100(a)(2)); 5 Whys and Ishikawa (src3, src4). Hours and the supplier share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for supplier root cause response
steps.description: The supplier investigates its own process under the corrective action request and replies with containment, root cause and corrective actions, often after reminders from the buyer.

error.defect_description: Supplier response is superficial and has to be challenged.

evidence.note: Supplier 8D turnaround of two to six weeks is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the CAPA plan
steps.description: The CAPA owner writes the actions that remove the cause, actions to prevent the same problem on similar products or lines, owners and due dates, and the criteria and timing for checking effectiveness.

error.defect_description: Effectiveness criteria vague, so the later check proves nothing.

evidence.note: Action plan with steps and deadlines and an effectiveness plan (src5); corrective versus preventive action (src3). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the CAPA plan
steps.description: The quality manager reviews the root cause evidence and the plan, checks that actions address the cause and that effectiveness can be measured, and approves it or sends it back for more investigation.

error.defect_description: Weak root cause approved under schedule pressure.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(3) and (b): identify actions needed to correct and prevent recurrence; activities and results documented

next.condition: root cause not supported, more investigation needed

evidence.note: Review and sign-off of investigation and outcomes (src5, 820.100). The 15% send-back rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Implement the corrective actions
steps.description: The CAPA owner makes the changes: fixture or tooling modifications, mistake-proofing, process parameter or inspection plan changes and revised work instructions, raising engineering changes where documents or designs must change and waiting for parts and approvals.

error.defect_description: Change made on one line but not on a similar line named in the plan.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(5): implement and record changes in methods and procedures

evidence.note: Implementing and recording changes (820.100(a)(5)); permanent corrective action (8D D6, src4). Waiting for engineering changes, parts and validation dominates; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Verify or validate the actions
steps.description: The quality engineer runs verification builds or, for process changes, protocol-based validation, measures the output against acceptance criteria and documents that the change works and does not harm the finished device.

error.defect_description: Sample too small to show the change works.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(4): verify or validate the corrective and preventive action and confirm no adverse effect on the finished device

evidence.note: Verification or validation of actions (820.100(a)(4)); verify permanent corrections (8D D5, src4). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Train operators on the change
steps.description: The production supervisor walks operators through the revised instructions at the workstation, has them sign the training record and checks the first runs under the new method.

error.defect_description: A shift is missed and keeps the old method.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(6): disseminate information on quality problems to those responsible

evidence.note: Dissemination of information to those directly responsible (820.100(a)(6)). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check effectiveness after the monitoring period
steps.description: After the agreed period, often two to three months or a set number of lots, the quality engineer pulls nonconformance, yield and complaint data for the affected process, compares it with the effectiveness criteria and records whether the problem has recurred.

error.defect_description: Recurrence missed because data were pulled for the wrong part family.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(4): ensure the action is effective (ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.5.2 verification of effectiveness)

evidence.note: Effectiveness verification with planned evidence and timing (src5, src7, 820.100(a)(4)). The monitoring window and 15% reopen rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the CAPA and report to management review
steps.description: The quality manager reviews the complete record, signs the closure, and the CAPA is counted in the monthly quality metrics and the management review summary.

error.defect_description: Closure signed with missing evidence, found at audit.

control.basis: 21 CFR 820.100(a)(7): submit information on quality problems and CAPA for management review

evidence.note: Sign-off and closure (src5); management review input (820.100(a)(7)). Wait is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Containment sweep of other stock
exceptions.description: Other lots, work in progress or finished goods may be affected, so inspectors sort them and the engineer checks whether any shipped.

exceptions.name: MRB asks for more data
exceptions.description: The board cannot decide and sends the package back for more measurements or analysis.

exceptions.name: Rework fails re-inspection
exceptions.description: Reworked parts still fail and return to the board for another disposition.

exceptions.name: Use-as-is disposition
exceptions.description: Material is accepted with a deviation, which needs a documented engineering justification and signature.

exceptions.name: Supplier root cause
exceptions.description: The cause lies at a supplier, so the CAPA waits for the supplier's 8D response.

exceptions.name: Root cause rejected at plan approval
exceptions.description: The quality manager finds the root cause unsupported and sends the CAPA back to investigation.

exceptions.name: CAPA not effective
exceptions.description: The problem recurs during the monitoring period and the investigation is reopened.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from detection to closure of the nonconformance report or, if escalated, the CAPA
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for a mid-size device plant

evidence.note: No source opened gave a measured nonconformance or CAPA closure time. p50 reflects reports closed after disposition within three to five weeks; p90 reflects CAPAs with a 60 to 120 day effectiveness window, longer than the common 90-day CAPA target noted in src5.

benchmarks.population: Common practice in device companies, as described by a QMS software vendor

evidence.note: src5 says a 90-day target is common but not required, and that thorough investigations may take longer.

benchmarks.unit: issues with CAPA systems at medical device companies in 2015
benchmarks.population: Medical device companies, as reported by src3 (the source does not say how the issues were counted)

evidence.note: Shows CAPA is a frequent inspection finding; older than the reference period.

pain_points.description: Root cause analysis stops at a restated problem or operator error, so CAPAs fail the plan approval or the effectiveness check and are reopened.

evidence.note: src5 warns teams often restate the problem instead of finding its cause.

pain_points.description: Material waits in the MRB area for the next board, for rework slots and for supplier return authorisations, tying up inventory and sometimes stopping the line.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common waits.

pain_points.description: CAPA implementation waits on engineering changes, tooling and validation, so many CAPAs exceed internal due dates.

evidence.note: src5 notes investigations and actions can run past a 90-day target.

pain_points.description: Nonconformance data sits in paper forms or a spreadsheet log, so repeat problems are spotted late and escalation to CAPA is inconsistent.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for plants without an integrated eQMS in 2019 to 2022.

pain_points.description: Every disposition and action needs a signature from a small number of authorised people, who become a bottleneck.

evidence.note: Defined authority and signatures are required by 820.90(b) and 820.100.

sources.title: 21 CFR Part 820 Quality System Regulation (Code of Federal Regulations, 2021 edition, Title 21 Volume 8)
sources.supports: 820.90(a): procedures for identification, documentation, evaluation, segregation and disposition of nonconforming product; evaluation includes determining the need for an investigation. 820.90(b): defined responsibility for review and authority for disposition; disposition documented with justification and signature for use of nonconforming product; rework procedures with retesting and reevaluation documented in the DHR. 820.100(a)(1)-(7) and (b): CAPA procedures covering analysis of quality data, investigation of cause, actions, verification or validation of effectiveness, implementation, dissemination and management review; all documented. 820.80(d): finished devices held until release is authorised.

sources.title: "Documented Information" in ISO 9001:2015 (handout with clause excerpts)
sources.supports: ISO 9001:2015 8.7: retain information describing the nonconformity, actions taken, concessions obtained and the authority deciding the action; 10.2.2: retain evidence of the nature of nonconformities, subsequent actions and results of corrective action.

sources.title: Corrective and preventive action
sources.supports: CAPA stages: identify problems from quality data, investigate root cause (5 Whys, Ishikawa, 8D), decide corrective and preventive actions, implement, review effectiveness; required for device makers by 21 CFR 820.100; over 450 CAPA system issues found at device companies in 2015.

sources.title: Eight disciplines problem solving
sources.supports: 8D steps: team, problem description (5W2H, is/is not), interim containment, root cause and escape point, verify permanent corrections, implement and validate corrective actions, prevent recurrence; developed at Ford in 1987 and standard in automotive supply chains.

sources.title: The CAPA Process: 15 Steps From Request to Effectiveness Verification
sources.supports: CAPA request, review board acceptance or rejection, tracking number, cross-functional team, containment, investigation, root cause, action plan with deadlines, implementation, review and sign-off, effectiveness verification plan and evidence; a fixed 90-day closure target is common but there is no regulatory timeline and thorough investigations may take longer.

sources.title: Case for Quality
sources.supports: FDA review of device quality data found common manufacturing risks; manufacturers that managed them had fewer complaints, opened fewer CAPAs and investigations and had lower quality-related costs.

sources.title: ISO 13485
sources.supports: ISO 13485:2016 quality management system for medical device design and manufacture; certification voluntary; 21 CFR 820 is the U.S. requirement; emphasises verifying the effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions.

sources.title: Nonconformity (quality)
sources.supports: Nonconformities are graded by severity (for example critical, major, minor); common causes include poor documentation, training, materials, tools and environment.

sources.title: May 2021 National Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates, United States
sources.supports: Median hourly wages: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers and Weighers 51-9061 $18.55; Industrial Engineers 17-2112 $45.82; Mechanical Engineers 17-2141 $45.82; Industrial Production Managers 11-3051 $49.59; First-Line Supervisors of Production 51-1011 $29.71; Miscellaneous Assemblers and Fabricators 51-2090 $17.59; Laborers and Freight, Stock and Material Movers 53-7062 $15.02; Buyers and Purchasing Agents 13-1020 $30.51.

sources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation - December 2021 (news release)
sources.supports: Manufacturing: total compensation $41.13 per hour, wages and salaries $27.38 (66.6%), benefits $13.76 (33.4%).

assumptions: One case is one nonconformance report. About 20% of reports are escalated and about 88% of those are accepted as CAPAs, so roughly 18% of cases (about nine CAPAs a month) run the full CAPA path; the rest close after disposition.

The cycle_time_days benchmark is the author's estimate because no source opened measured closure times. The simulated median is driven by reports closed without CAPA; the 90th percentile is driven by CAPAs and their effectiveness window.
Desk work share is low for detection, segregation, sorting, rework and re-inspection, and partial for MRB, investigation, implementation and verification, which mix shop-floor and desk work.
The MRB and CAPA board steps record total attendee minutes under the quality manager's role.

Regulatory controls cite the Quality System Regulation 21 CFR 820 as in force in 2019 to 2022 (since February 2026 FDA's Quality Management System Regulation incorporates ISO 13485 instead); ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 clauses are named where they set the same rule.
Loaded hourly cost is the BLS May 2021 national median wage for the nearest SOC code times 1.7 (1.50 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for manufacturing, about 1.13 overhead by author estimate).
Disposition mix, escalation rate, rework rates and most times are tier C estimates.
